```plato

//==
// # The solver view of a body
//
// `RigidBody3D` is the AUTHORING record: it names a material-facing mass, an
// inertia tensor about the centre of mass, a motion kind, and damping rates. The
// integrator and the contact solver want none of that spelling. They want, per
// body, the quantities that appear in an impulse: where the centre of mass is,
// how it is oriented, how fast it is going, and how much velocity one
// newton-second of impulse buys. `SolverBody3D` is that reading of a
// `RigidBody3D` — derived from it by `SolverBody`, never a second authoring
// vocabulary.
//
// Two things collapse in the translation, and both are deliberate:
//
//   * MOTION KIND BECOMES ZERO. A `Static` or `Kinematic` body is a body with
//     `InverseMass` and `InverseInertia` of zero: an impulse changes nothing.
//     The solver then has no case analysis at all, and no branch that a static
//     body could take by accident.
//   * THE INERTIA TENSOR BECOMES ITS PRINCIPAL DIAGONAL. Every primitive whose
//     inertia this library computes is diagonal in its own frame, so the world
//     inverse inertia never has to be assembled or inverted as a full matrix:
//     `I^-1 t` is a rotation into the body frame, three multiplies, and a
//     rotation back (`AngularResponse` in `rigid-dynamics.library.plato`). A body
//     whose tensor is genuinely non-diagonal must be given in its principal frame
//     first (`PrincipalInertia`), which is where that approximation is stated.

// One body as the integrator and the contact solver read it: field for field a
// `RigidBody3D` with the two things a solver cannot use — the motion kind and the
// inertia tensor — replaced by the two it can: a zeroable inverse mass, and the
// reciprocals of the three principal moments.
//
// Center is the world position of the centre of mass, in meters; Orientation maps
// the body's PRINCIPAL axes onto world axes; Velocity is the world-frame twist
// ABOUT THE CENTRE OF MASS (linear in meters per second, angular in radians per
// second); InverseMass is in reciprocal kilograms and InverseInertia holds the
// reciprocals of the three principal moments, in reciprocal
// kilogram-square-meters, with zero in either meaning "immovable in that
// respect"; LinearDamping and AngularDamping are the exponential velocity decay
// rates of the authoring record, in units of one per second; GravityScale is its
// dimensionless gravity multiplier.
type SolverBody3D
    implements IValue
{
    Center: Point3D;
    Orientation: Quaternion;
    Velocity: SpatialVelocity3D;
    InverseMass: Number;
    InverseInertia: Vector3D;
    LinearDamping: Number;
    AngularDamping: Number;
    GravityScale: Number;
}
```
